scenes.name: Hook: it would hear you tomorrow
Brainwaves of a woman in love

lines.text: If you said hello to this spacecraft right now, it would hear you tomorrow.
lines.delivery: Intimate, a half-smile, as if telling a secret. Let 'tomorrow' land softly but clearly.
Documentary, warm. A little pride on 'Voyager one'.

lines.text: On {November 18, 2026|November eighteenth, twenty twenty-six}, it crosses a full light-day from home.
lines.delivery: The milestone. Slow down on 'a full light-day', then let it breathe.

lines.text: It still calls home on about the power of a fridge light bulb.
lines.delivery: Amused admiration. 'A fridge light bulb' should sound almost absurd.

lines.text: In {1990|nineteen ninety}, it turned around and took a photo of us: a pale blue dot.
lines.delivery: Quieter. A beat before 'a pale blue dot', and say it gently, like a name.

lines.text: It also carries a golden record, for whoever finds it.
lines.delivery: Wonder, a little mystery on 'whoever finds it'.

lines.text: Music. Greetings in {55|fifty-five} languages. A heartbeat.
lines.delivery: A list, each item its own small picture. Slow and soft on 'a heartbeat'.

lines.text: And the brainwaves of a woman who had just fallen in love.
lines.delivery: The turn. Tender, unhurried; smile on 'just fallen in love'.

lines.text: Ann Druyan. The man she loved, Carl Sagan, led the project.
lines.delivery: Warm, matter-of-fact. Names said with respect.

lines.text: In {40,000|forty thousand} years, it will drift past another star, still carrying their love story.
lines.delivery: Expansive, then intimate: the scale of time against something very small and human.

lines.text: And for now... it's still listening.
lines.delivery: Almost a whisper. The video loops straight back to 'If you said hello to this spacecraft right now…'
